generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The change from using `Unpooled.unmodifiableBuffer` to creating a new instance of `ReadOnlyByteBuf` or its subclasses is correct for ensuring that the returned buffers are truly read-only. However, this change introduces several new classes (`ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf`, `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf`) which could increase complexity and maintenance overhead. Ensure these new classes do not introduce any performance regressions.

The new test case `testReadOnlyRelease` is valuable for ensuring that read-only buffers are correctly released and do not affect the reference count of their parent buffer. However, ensure that `newBuffer(8)` returns a buffer that can be safely converted to a read-only buffer in this context.

The introduction of `ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf` and `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf` is appropriate for maintaining immutability, but the repeated code in these subclasses (especially `asReadOnly`, `slice`, `duplicate`, `isWritable`) can be refactored to reduce duplication. Consider creating a common base class or using composition to share this functionality.

The addition of multiple test cases (`testReadOnlyRelease`, `testDuplicateRelease`, `testSliceRelease`, etc.) is comprehensive and ensures that different scenarios involving read-only buffers are covered. However, the repeated pattern in these tests (e.g., setting `writerIndex` and calling `testRelease`) can be refactored into a parameterized test to reduce redundancy.

review_comment: The reason why read-only ByteBuffers are needed in the SslHandler use case is to avoid mutating the buffer. JDK's SSLEngine will mutate the input buffer with an in-place encryption reusing the input buffer unless the buffer is read-only. The support for read-only ByteBuffers in JDK's SSLEngine was added as a result of a bug reported by @chrisvest, more details in comment https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14069#issuecomment-2129279047 .
